captured_note: Ported from the capture's self-contained methods/8_split_brain, specifically its AlexNet path (model.py's SplitBrainAlexNet/SplitBrainModel, dataset.py, evaluate_linear.py). These are the lab's own implementation of Zhang, Isola & Efros (CVPR 2017) Split-Brain Autoencoders. The capture directory number (8) equals this method's number in the Step 1&2 list (see docs/PORTING_ROADMAP.md); the ported directory is zero-padded to 08_split_brain to match the other single-digit methods.

paper.title: Split-Brain Autoencoders: Unsupervised Learning by Cross-Channel Prediction

scope: The AlexNet path is ported: an image is converted to CIE Lab and split into its L and ab channels; two cross-channel AlexNet branches predict one from the other -- net1 maps L (1-ch) to the quantised ab channels (313 bins), net2 maps ab (2-ch) to the quantised L channel (50 bins), each an encoder + a small deconv decoder producing per-pixel class logits. The loss is the sum of the two cross-entropies. The capture's ViT step 2 (a channel-split ViT, timm) is EXCLUDED, as in every port.
encoder: encoder.pt is the two branch encoders (net1.encoder.* / net2.encoder.*). The two deconv decoders are pretext machinery and are excluded. extract_features(l, ab) concatenates both encoders' spatially-averaged features (256 + 256 = 512-d) -- the representation the linear probe reads.
linear_eval: Reads the trained encoder.pt and probes the concatenated 512-d feature (both frozen encoders reading the L and ab channels), a genuine learned representation, so the number is comparable. Follows the lab's shared ARSSL probe (mean-centre + L2-normalise, single linear layer, SGD momentum + cosine, top1/top5) rather than the capture's own 1000-way head, so the number is comparable across the ported methods.

vendored_constant.note: The 313 in-gamut ab-bin centres; the capture pins this exact sha256 (AB_CODEBOOK_SHA256 in its constants.py) and its copy is a symlink into the cluster's LIVE_ROOT (not in the snapshot), so the port vendors the authoritative constant (the same file as 03_colorization). Loaded with a sha256 check; there is no runtime download.

rewritten_during_the_port: only the AlexNet path is ported; the channel-split ViT step 2 (timm) is excluded, so the port has no timm dependency

the RGB->CIE Lab conversion and the ab/L quantisation are pure numpy; the capture's dataset used scipy.spatial.cKDTree and skimage.color, but its own comment states the released ab target IS NumPy argmin (cKDTree only accelerates it and is corrected to match), so the port uses numpy argmin and depends on neither scipy nor scikit-image, keeping the torch-only closure
the 313 ab-bin codebook is vendored and sha256-verified on load (the capture's copy is a symlink into the cluster's LIVE_ROOT); a missing or altered constant errors loudly

the capture ships no AlexNet step-1 recipe (its train.py trains the ViT step 2 under DDP + AdamW with a canonical contract); the port owns a thin single-process fp32 loop with a plain Adam optimiser, its knobs exposed in the config
the loss is the sum of the two per-pixel cross-entropies, with each target downsampled (nearest) to the decoder output resolution, as in the lab's training loop
the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext loss and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch)
the training loop drops the upstream DistributedDataParallel and TensorBoard so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged, single-process fp32
DATA_ROOT is the dataset root; step-1 reads its train/ subdirectory (unified data-root convention via adapterlib.dataset_split_dir).
